thinking: Found a known hazard: the ledger endpoint lacks an idempotency key, so retrying an already-processed request risks double-posting an invoice. I'll only retry failures where the request definitely never reached the ledger (connect timeouts), skipping read timeouts and connection resets.

`finalize()` in `src/billing/invoices.py` now makes up to 3 attempts, but it only retries connect timeouts, not every network error. I haven't run it or added tests.

I held back because an EngramDB hazard note says the ledger endpoint has no idempotency key. If a request reaches the ledger and the response is then lost (read timeout, connection reset), a retry would post the invoice twice. A connect timeout means the request never got through, so retrying it is safe. After the third failed attempt the original `ConnectTimeout` is re-raised, and each retry logs `invoice_finalize_retry`.

Read timeouts, connection resets and other `ConnectionError`s still fail immediately, so the original intermittent failures may only be partly fixed. If most of them are read timeouts or resets, retrying safely needs either an idempotency key on the ledger side or a lookup of the invoice before each retry. Tell me which you'd prefer and I can build it. Retrying every network error blindly is the one option I'd avoid, since it risks double-posting.
